name: Pakistan Army Museum (public exterior only)
assumptions: Front bearing set to 3 degrees, not the dossier's 93: 93 is the long axis, and the north edge of the OSM outline has the end, centre and recess pattern of the head-on photo.
Scale from the head-on photo tied to the 56.6 m OSM front (about 0.05 m per pixel). Height 12 m to the blocking course, column tops 9.4 m: estimates, no published height.
The front is built symmetric about the mid point of its OSM width; the OSM trace of the central section sits about 2.4 m to the west of that axis.
Current grey rendered finish taken from the recent head-on photo; an older oblique photo shows red brick end blocks with cast letters, treated as superseded.
Depth of the columns behind the front row (about 2.8 m at the inner pair, 6 m at the end pair) inferred from apparent height in one wide-angle photo.
Rear and side elevations were not photographed: plain grey render with plinth, string course and cornice, no windows invented.
The rear outline is the OSM footprint, including its projecting east, west and south arms.
Glazed barrel roof: shape from the interior atrium photo; its plan position (centre of the outline), 22 by 17 m size and 3.4 m rise are estimates.
Two rooftop heads left of the axis: only their tops show in one photo; position and size estimated.
Statue: size from photos, figure simplified to massing. Sits at the top of the steps per the head-on photo; a close photo may place it slightly lower.
Field guns on the lawn: red-wheeled type read from one small view; form simplified. Position about 3.4 m ahead of the plinth, estimated.

Courtyard aircraft and vehicles (Dawn) are not modelled: the aircraft photos show them under the glazed atrium, not visible outside. Tanks and the old anti-aircraft gun are absent from the recent front photo.
Urdu line above the English sign left off: unreadable at photo resolution. Crescent and swords on the dark windows simplified.
Night glow colours are estimated; no night photo found.
